hypothesis: The DAEMON (supervisor) process retains freed-but-resident heap after daemon-side session reads/relays because #2872's trims all live in worker-role paths and none in the supervisor: the supervisor relays every routed worker response through a serde_json Value tree (reader from_slice -> DaemonResponse -> response_line -> client write) and the catalog scan folds a parse tree per file line, but never returns the freed pages, so one grown session's CLI-path relay (+71MiB for a 9.47MiB get_messages; +42MiB more for a routed attach) and every grown catalog scan stay at the arena high-water for the daemon's lifetime.
approach: (1) BASELINE at tip 7064d039a: TUI-first bench battery with per-proc sidecar (daemon RSS flat 23.5-24.9 across 1/2/5/10MiB + compacted, n=5-10/shape, noise band 1.19MiB); census3 replica (daemon-first TUI: 46.4-51.1 at BOTH +3s and +12s - the anomaly is the launch shape, not deferred reads); daemon-direct wire probes (no TUI) with per-phase daemon+worker RSS/PSS/smaps captures across shapes; throwaway env-gated census instrument (PRIME_DR_CENSUS) for per-frame/per-read in-process attribution. (2) CANDIDATE: mirror #2872's pattern at the two daemon-side phase boundaries - write_line reports serialized bytes + the client write loop drops the tree and trims at >=1MiB; the catalog scan trims at its join (live per-file cache states untouched). +30/-9, supervisor.rs only. (3) PAIRS: same-VM sequential B/C/B/C with sha-asserted atomic binary swaps, fresh-daemon trials, per-arm fsync-regime probes, single-driver guards, calibration pre/mid/post; TUI-first bench no-regression arms; gates at the head. Fold history: 7064d039a -> folded c7ca05f10 (merge 726c1d67b, no conflict) -> folded 1507d399b incl. #2879/#2884/#2880/#2887 (merge ddc4ee946, no conflict; post-fold re-diff vs each merge-base = the 3 hunks intact, supervisor.rs only).
parity_notes: Allocator plumbing only - no data, capability, protocol, wire, prompt, or user-visible behavior changes. The trim runs AFTER the client frame is written and its Value tree dropped; wire bytes are identical. Non-glibc/non-Linux builds are no-ops via pa_types::memory_release (cfg linux/gnu): macOS arm64 + non-glibc unchanged; shipped Linux x86_64 glibc2.35+ and aarch64 covered. The TUI's direct worker transport never produces >=1MiB supervisor-routed lines, so the TUI flow is behaviorally untouched (bench arms overlap at ~24MiB daemon). At the folded merge-base the #2878 split's supervisor/clients.rs is committed but not yet declared as a module - the live client loop (and these hunks) remains in supervisor.rs; when the split's later step flips mod clients; on, the write-path hunks re-home to clients.rs (the catalog trim stays with handle_saved_session_list). No manager/window/worker files touched (worker-rss territory); no fold internals touched (catalog-second-parse territory).
